summary: The bounce became a trend today. One day after Thursday reversed the hawkish Fed selloff, the tape followed through and pushed higher. NQ rose 1.84 percent to 29,960, ES gained 1.14 percent to 7,726, and December gold added 0.82 percent to 4,416, and all three stayed above the trend stops they reclaimed yesterday. Those stops are now rising underneath price. The tell: NQ closed near its highs at 29,960, just under the 30,000 wall, instead of fading late like it did Thursday. Crude was again the lone holdout. It spiked to 103.4 overnight, then collapsed to close 99.54, down 1.53 percent and still below its stop. VIX eased further to 14.81. All of this landed on quarterly quad witching, so read the strong close with a little caution.

risk.note: Throttle NORMAL with a weekend and quad witching caveat. The Fed event risk is behind us and the trend followed through a second day, but today's strength rode expiry flow, and Monday opens after a weekend and after the Bank of Japan meeting. A gap can reprice the tape before the levels trade. Week ahead: minor Chicago Fed activity index Monday, flash PMIs midweek. Let Monday's levels confirm before adding risk.

psychology: Yesterday the market bounced. Today it followed through. That sequence turns a one-day reversal into a trend, and the standout detail is the close. Thursday NQ ran to its highs and gave the last two hours back. Today it ran to its highs and held them into the bell, even through the mechanical flow of a quad witching Friday. That is a stronger signal than the raw percent gain. The discipline part: a strong Friday close is not a reason to carry oversized risk over a weekend. Expiry flow can pin price near big strikes, and 30,000 is a huge strike wall overhead, so some of today's push is mechanics, not pure conviction. Monday opens after a weekend and after the Bank of Japan meeting wrapped. Respect the trend, keep size honest into the gap.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN
fullReport.html:
NQ opened into a tight 46 point range: high 29,845.25, low 29,798.75. The first move was a downside break, confirmed at 13:45 UTC at 29,776. That break failed. Price reversed up, closed back inside the range, and trended to a 29,994 high, finishing 29,960 well above NYVWAP 29,764. The clean opening signal was a failed downside break that flipped into a trend up, a reminder that the first break on a busy open is often the trap.

For Monday, HTA OPEN eligibility is HOF, MID and BNC; BIR skips Mondays. The HOF 12:00 to 14:00 ET dead zone applies. Conditional and educational only.

fullReport.title: Momentum Breakout (Regime Filter)
fullReport.html: E3v2 Momentum Long stayed on the board. The regime filter is armed because both indices closed above their rising stops, and momentum carried price into the close near the highs. The messy part was the open, where the first opening-range break was down and failed before price reversed up. The clean version of a fresh long is a hold above the 30,000 wall and today's 29,994 high on two hourly closes. Quad witching added noise, so let a fresh Monday break prove itself before sizing in.

fullReport.title: AVWAP Deviation Band Reversal (MNQ)
fullReport.html: AVWAP center 29,798, close 29,960 sits about 1.9 sigma above the mean. Bands: plus 2 sigma 29,971, plus 3 sigma 30,057, minus 2 sigma 29,626, minus 3 sigma 29,540. Sigma widened to about 86, the opposite of Thursday's compressed 19, because price trended one direction. The RTH high 29,994 tagged just past the plus 2 sigma band, but on a clean trend day a band tag is a with-trend event, not a fade. Volume is unavailable on the continuous contract, so this is price only. Wait for a two-way range before trusting a fresh fade.
